LinkedIn · croatianferries.com · series post 2

Week one: 3,164 pages to get indexed, 7 requests a day, and position 5 for a camera nobody aimed at.

Episode 2, ferry only, and rebuilt around your steer: the SEO edge from the beginning. The site has been live under a week, so the post now opens on the week-one problem - the sitemap going from 316 pages to 3,164 in one deploy, the fact that Google's API reports index status but cannot request indexing, the roughly 7-a-day manual quota and the priority order it gets spent in, and the 09:40 job that reads the live sitemap and writes the tally onto the issue (en 0/45 to 43/45). The rankings are now the payoff rather than the subject: the cameras and the named port pairs are what a site with no authority actually wins. Every number is from today's snapshot, issue #23 and commit 273a48b - nothing reused from the handoff. The GA4 story is out entirely: it happened on zazet-solutions and cannot carry an episode about the ferry site.

The post, Hebrew

2,710 characters (cap 3,000). אמ!לק opener with the episode frame, the age of the site and the camera number in line 1; episode 1 named in paragraph 2; then 316 to 3,164, the 7-a-day quota, the daily job and the 0/45 to 43/45 line, the embarrassing baseline, the head terms that are nowhere, what does rank, the cameras, the truncated titles, and the 16-of-99 discipline.

אמ!לק -> מנסה לבנות את הפורטל הימי הכי טוב בקרואטיה, פרק 2: האתר באוויר פחות משבוע, וכבר מדורג במקום 5 בגוגל על מצלמת הנמל במרג. לא ניסיתי להגיע לשם, והכותרת של העמוד בכלל לא הזכירה מצלמה.

בפרק 1 הפידבק הגיע מבני אדם, 52 קבוצות פייסבוק והתגובות בתור באג טראקר. הפעם הלכתי לשאול את גוגל, ושבוע ראשון של אתר הוא בעיה אחרת לגמרי: איך אתה בכלל גורם למנוע חיפוש לדעת שאתה קיים.

הדיפלוי שהוסיף את עמודי האיים ואת עמודי הזוגות העלה את הסייטמאפ מ-316 עמודים ל-3,164. יפה. עכשיו תנסה להכניס אותם פנימה.

וכאן הפרט שאף אחד לא מספר לך: ה-API של גוגל יודע להגיד לך אם עמוד מאונדקס, אבל הוא לא יודע לבקש אינדוקס. הבקשה היא קליק ידני בממשק, והמכסה היומית היא בערך 7-8 עמודים. 3,164 חלקי 7 ליום זה קצת יותר משנה, אז זה לא המסלול. הסייטמאפ עושה את העבודה בקצב של גוגל, ואת 7 הבקשות היומיות אני מוציא לפי סדר עדיפויות: קודם עמודי האיים באנגלית, אחר כך איטלקית, גרמנית, קרואטית, ועמודי הזוגות בסוף לפי נפח חיפוש משוער.

הדבר היחיד שנשאר זה למדוד, כל יום, בלי לשכוח. יש ג'וב שרץ כל בוקר ב-9:40, קורא את הסייטמאפ החי (אף פעם לא רשימה שהקלדתי ביד, כי רשימה כזאת מתיישנת ביום), שואל את סרץ' קונסול מה מצב האינדוקס של כל עמוד אי, וכותב את הספירה כתגובה על האישיו. ככה זה נראה:

לפני: en 0/45 · it 0/45 · de 0/45 · hr 0/45
היום: en 43/45 · it 20/45 · de 32/45 · hr 15/45

והמספרים של החיפוש עצמו מביכים ואני שם אותם על השולחן: קליק אחד. 172 חשיפות. זה מה שמגיע לאתר בשבוע הראשון שלו.

אבל בתוך 172 החשיפות האלה יש מפה. ציפיתי לראות את הקווים הגדולים: ספליט-סופטאר, המעבר הכי עמוס בקרואטיה, נמצא במקום 57. "מעבורות קרואטיה" בגרמנית, 49. "מספליט לדוברובניק", 67. אין סיכוי שאתר בן שבוע ינצח על הביטויים האלה.

מה שכן עלה למעלה, אף אחד לא כיוון אליו: hak merag במקום 5, hak kamera porozina במקום 8, hak kamera brestova במקום 9. וגם סומרטין-מקרסקה 6, זאדאר-פרקו 9, דומינצ'ה-קורצ'ולה 8. כלומר: זוג נמלים מסוים בשם מלא, ומצלמות.

אלה אנשים שמחפשים את המצלמה החיה של הנמל לפני שהם יוצאים מהבית, לראות כמה ארוך התור. אני מטמיע את המצלמות של רשות התחבורה הקרואטית בעמוד של כל נמל שיש לו אחת. לאף אתר מעבורות מתחרה אין את זה בכלל. זה הדבר היחיד שיש לי ואין לאף אחד אחר, הוא כבר בעשירייה הראשונה, והוא היה בלתי נראה: הכותרת לא אמרה את המילה מצלמה.

וכשהלכתי לתקן את זה נפל משהו גדול יותר. Trajekti i katamarani iz luke Zadar Liburnska obala · plovidbeni red · Croatian Ferries. 87 תווים, וגוגל מציג בערך 60. לעמודי הקווים היה שומר אורך מזמן, לעמודי הנמלים פשוט אף פעם לא נתתי את אותו שומר. 278 מתוך 396 הכותרות היו חתוכות. עכשיו 6.

ו-16 נמלים מתוך 99 אומרים "מצלמה חיה" בכותרת. ה-16 נבדקים מול מפת המצלמות בזמן הבילד ולא הוכרזו ביד, כדי ש-83 הנמלים שאין להם לא יבטיחו כלום.

SEO לוקח שלושה-ארבעה שבועות להירשם, אז אין לי עדיין שום תוצאה להראות ואני לא הולך להעמיד פנים אחרת. הסקריפטים, טבלת השאילתות המלאה והכותרות לפני ואחרי, בתגובה הראשונה.

The post, English

2,982 characters.

TL;DR -> trying to build the best maritime portal in Croatia, episode 2: the site has been live under a week and already ranks 5th on Google for the live port camera at Merag. I never tried to rank for it, and the title did not contain the word camera.

In episode 1 the feedback came from people: 52 Facebook groups, the comments as my bug tracker. This time I asked Google, and the first week of a site is a different problem entirely: how do you get a search engine to know you exist at all.

The deploy that added the island and port-pair pages took the sitemap from 316 pages to 3,164. Now try getting them in.

Here is the part nobody tells you: Google's API can tell you whether a page is indexed, but it cannot ask for indexing. That is a manual click in the UI, capped at about 7 to 8 pages a day. 3,164 divided by 7 is over a year, so that is not the route. The sitemap does the work on Google's schedule, and the 7 daily requests get spent in priority order: English island pages first, then Italian, German, Croatian, pairs last.

What is left is to measure it daily without forgetting. A job runs each morning at 09:40, reads the live sitemap (never a hand-typed list, that goes stale in a day), asks Search Console the index state of every island page, and writes the tally onto the issue:

Before: en 0/45 - it 0/45 - de 0/45 - hr 0/45
Today:  en 43/45 - it 20/45 - de 32/45 - hr 15/45

The search numbers are embarrassing, so here they are: one click. 172 impressions. About what a site deserves in week one.

But inside those 172 impressions there is a map. I expected the big routes. Split - Supetar, the busiest crossing in Croatia, sits at 57. "Ferries Croatia" in German, 49. "Dubrovnik to Split ferry schedule", 67. A week old site is not winning those.

What did come up, nobody aimed at: hak merag at 5, hak kamera porozina at 8, hak kamera brestova at 9. And Sumartin - Makarska at 6, Zadar - Preko at 9. Which is to say: cameras, and one specific pair of ports named in full.

Those are people checking the port's live camera before leaving the house, to see how long the queue is. I embed the Croatian transport authority cameras on the page of every port that has one, and no competing ferry site does this. The one thing I have that nobody else has was already in the top ten, and invisible: the title never said the word camera.

Going to fix that turned up something bigger. A typical port title ran 87 characters; Google shows about 60. Route pages have had a length guard for a while, port pages never got it. 278 of 396 titles were cut off in the results. Now 6.

And 16 ports out of 99 now say "live camera" in the title. Those 16 are resolved against the camera map at build time rather than asserted, so the other 83 promise nothing they do not have.

SEO takes three to four weeks to register, so I have nothing to show yet and will not pretend otherwise. The scripts, the full query table and the titles before and after, in the first comment.

02 · Hero image - pick one

What your own numbers say. Your 133,171 post carried a single image that WAS its subject - the Wiz logo itself, not a description of it. Your 25,185 post had no famous name and ran on one measured number. Those are the two shapes that have worked, and here they are 5-HE and 1-HE. On episode 1 you took the artifact shape over the claim shape for the first time.

Which one here. 5-HE, on the same tiebreaker as last time: line 1 already spends "position 5 at Merag", so the number hero repeats the hook while the sawn-off title adds the thing the text has not reached yet. A cold reader seeing a real page title chopped mid-word wants to know whose site that is.

The honest risk. 5-HE is a defect in your own product at poster size on your own feed. On the launch post you deleted that kind of line yourself. The argument that this is different: it is fixed, the post is about finding it, and it is not a launch - but if it reads as a reason not to trust the site, take 1-HE, which is not a consolation prize.

03 · How much indexing plumbing stays in the post?

The 3,164 pages, the 7-a-day quota and the 09:40 job are now the first half. It is the most useful material for anyone else launching a site, and it is also the least dramatic thing in the post.

Keep all of it RECOMMENDED

This is what you asked for and it is the part nobody writes down: that the API will tell you the status but will not ask for the crawl, that the ask is a manual click capped at 7 a day, and that the answer is therefore the sitemap plus a priority queue. The 0/45 to 43/45 line is the only real result in the whole post.

Keep it, drop the priority order

Cuts the "English first, then Italian, German, Croatian, pairs last" sentence. Saves about 150 characters and loses the one detail that shows it was thought about rather than fired off.

Two lines, then straight to the rankings

"3,164 pages, 7 requests a day, a job that counts every morning." Faster to the cameras, but then the post is a rankings post again and the week-one angle is gone.

04 · The truncated-titles section

278 of 396 of your own pages were broken in search results for two months. It is the strongest material in the post and it is also a bug in your own product, which the ledger says you cut.

Keep as drafted RECOMMENDED

It is now the second half rather than the spine, which lowers the risk. The croatian-ferries rule was about a launch post, where an unfixed bug is a reason not to click. This is fixed, shipped and tested, and finding it is the payoff of the whole post. Without it the post is only "the long tail ranks", which everyone already knows.

Demote to one line

"On the way I found that 278 of 396 port titles were cut off in Google, and fixed it." Keeps the number, loses the 87-character example that makes it concrete.

Cut it, blog only

Post ends on the cameras. Cleanest, and about 500 characters shorter, but the post loses its second half and its only real defect.

05 · The one click

"One click. 172 impressions. A full month." Fourth consecutive post with a drafted-in embarrassing number, and the first three all survived your edit untouched.

Keep it RECOMMENDED

It is what makes the rest readable as investigation rather than a success story, and it is the one thing in the post a model would not write about itself.

Keep the numbers, drop "embarrassing"

Report them flat and let the reader judge.

Cut the baseline

Go straight to the rankings. Stronger looking, weaker post, and someone will ask.

06 · The takeaway line near the end

"I stopped trying to rank for Croatia ferries and started building around what already works." On episode 1 you rewrote every generalisation back into first person - this one already is first person, but it is still the closest thing in the post to advice.

Keep as drafted RECOMMENDED

It says what you did, not what the reader should do, and it names the two concrete things: a page per named pair, a camera on every port that has one.

Write it yourself

Your version of this line was the best line in episode 1. If you have one, mine goes.

Cut it

End on the 16-of-99 discipline and the three-to-four weeks. Less tidy, more honest.

Honest notes, and what I checked

  • The indexing numbers are from issue #23 and ops/gsc/indexed.py: sitemap 316 → 3,164 discovered, reported Success on 5 Sept; first day's inspection requests all rejected on quota; the launchd job com.ferry-watch.gsc runs 09:40 daily, pulls island URLs from the live sitemap and posts the tally. Day one en 0/45 · it 0/45 · de 0/45 · hr 0/45; today en 43/45 · it 20/45 · de 32/45 · hr 15/45. The post says "about 7-8 a day" because that is what the quota actually behaves like, and the script's own docstring is the source for "the API cannot request indexing".
  • The site's age: the post says under a week, which matches the public launch. The GSC window (7 Aug – 3 Sept) predates that - the domain was crawlable before the launch post - so the 172 impressions are the pre-launch trickle. If you would rather not blur those two, say so and I will time-box the sentence.
  • Every query and position is read from the snapshot, not from the handoff: ~/.claude/skills/analytics/ledger/snapshots/2026-09-06.json, GSC 2026-08-07 to 2026-09-03. 1 click, 172 impressions, CTR 0.58%, average position 20.7. hak merag 5 (2 impressions), hak kamera porozina 8, hak kamera brestova 9, gazenica brbinj trajekt 7, domince korcula 8, fähre sumartin makarska fahrplan 9, fähre zadar dugi otok fahrplan 11. Head terms: fähre kroatien 49, fähre split supetar 57, dubrovnik to split ferry schedule 67.
  • The title numbers are from the commit, and the tests pass: ferry-watch 273a48b, 278 of 396 over-length down to 6, 16 of 99 ports carry a camera and are resolved against the camera map at build time, 146 site tests green, deployed to Cloudflare Pages.
  • Every position here is a tiny sample. hak merag is 2 impressions; most of the rest are 1. The post says which pages rank, never how much traffic they bring, because 172 impressions cannot support the second claim. This is also why the "position 57" retraction is in the blog: it is the same mistake, made by me, three paragraphs earlier in the same run.
  • No traffic win is claimed anywhere, in the post or the blog. SEO takes three to four weeks; the post says so out loud and promises nothing.
  • The GA4 near-miss is not in this post. It is a zazet-solutions story and an episode about the maritime portal cannot carry it. It is also a post about model behaviour, which the ledger flags as the risky genre. It keeps until you want a standalone post about it.
  • The two retractions are in the blog, not the post - the n=1 position and the Cloudflare 301 that the redirect file never showed. They are the most useful material for a technical reader and they slow the post down.
  • Still open and named in the blog: 98 of 172 impressions come from Croatia while the /de/ tree is what ranks, and www serves a full duplicate at 200 with a canonical mitigating it.
  • Blog is live at gal.tidhar.org.il/blog/ferry-analytics/ once pushed, with the full query table, both retractions, the title before and after, and what is still open. og.png is 5-EN until you pick.
